overview: The City Council and Community Development Board held a joint public hearing to deliberate on proposed zoning amendments for the Boston Avenue Neighborhood Corridor District. The bodies reached consensus on several land-use definitions and directed consultants to model specific massing and boundary options for a final vote at the next meeting.

items.title: Public Comment
items.summary: Neighbors expressed concerns regarding home ownership, traffic, rodent control, and the potential impact of purpose-built student housing on neighborhood character.

items.title: Parking for Lodgers
items.summary: Approved a motion to reduce the parking requirement to zero for the accessory use of renting up to two rooms to lodgers.

items.title: Doggy Daycares and Medical Offices
items.summary: Voted to require a special permit for doggy daycares while maintaining small neighborhood medical offices as a by-right use in all sub-districts.

items.title: Motor Vehicle Service Stations
items.summary: Confirmed that new gas stations and motor vehicle repair shops will remain prohibited uses within the proposed corridor district.

items.title: Marijuana-Related Uses
items.summary: Approved changing marijuana-related uses to 'not allowed' in the district to maintain consistency with existing city-wide licensing ordinances.

items.title: Purpose-Built Student Housing Standards
items.summary: Directed the zoning consultants to draft a formal definition and use standards for private, taxable student housing, specifically excluding fraternities and sororities.

items.title: Height, Boundary, and Shadow Study Analysis
items.summary: Reviewed shadow studies for sub-district BA3 and considered proposals to adjust boundaries near St. Clement's and certain residential blocks in BA1.

items.title: Final Options for Sub-District Modeling
items.summary: Directed the consultant to prepare three specific boundary and height modeling options for sub-districts BA1, BA2, and BA3 for final deliberation on June 24th.
